transcript:
[00:00] Sofia Ramos: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we can start. Uh, we scheduled an hour, so we'll try to keep to 45-ish for the main topics and leave 15 for Q&A. Thanks Anika, Marco, Ravi, Priya for joining from Skybridge.
[00:25] Anika Patel: Yeah thanks, Sofia. Excited to dig in; we've had some internal ask to get Redwood listed on the Skybridge marketplace and also figure out a recommended reference arch for customers who want a private deployment.
[00:38] Sofia Ramos: Perfect. Quick intros — I'll hand to Ethan to do a high-level of what Redwood will need for a marketplace listing and then we can go into the VPC wiring and packaging.
[00:46] Ethan Li: Hi all, Ethan from Redwood SE. Quick TL;DR: listing needs metadata (screenshots, logos), billing/metering integration details, a deployment artifact (Terraform/Helm or AMI/container with runbook), and security/compliance docs. For private deployments we recommend a reference arch that supports VPC peering or private link, KMS integration, and a model of dedicated vs hosted fallback.
[01:10] Marco Silva: When you say "metering integration" — are you expecting Skybridge to call back to Redwood for usage, or to consume a usage report? How does that typically work?
[01:21] Ethan Li: Good q. Two patterns: marketplace-managed billing where Skybridge handles billing and sends metered reports (we provide usage reporting API), or direct billing where Redwood invoices customers and Skybridge is just a discovery channel. We prefer marketplace-managed for enterprise customers because it centralizes invoices, but both are supported.
[01:41] Ravi Menon: For our customers we often need usage detail down to tokens or inference units, is that something your reporting API provides?
[01:49] Ethan Li: Yes, we can emit per-route per-model usage logs; it's an authenticated report endpoint or periodic CSV export — we can share the spec.
[01:58] Anika Patel: On the deployment side, our marketplace supports a SaaS listing and a bring-your-own-license private listing. What does Redwood recommend for the reference arch?
[02:09] Ethan Li: For SaaS it's straightforward. For private / BYOL we recommend two patterns: 1) VPC peering with a lightweight control-plane in Skybridge and customer-managed compute in their VPC that runs Redwood's inference runtime in a containerized form; or 2) an on-prem packaged appliance (Helm/Terraform + images) that customers deploy into their cluster with a private control plane. We have a reference Terraform module and Helm chart we can provide.
[02:39] Priya Rao: On the security front, we need clarity on key management. Can your private option integrate with customer KMS/HSM?
[02:48] Sofia Ramos: Yes, Redwood Private supports KMS integrations — AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, and customer HSMs for private deployments. The control plane can be configured to use the customer KMS keys; we also support envelope encryption and audit logs.
[03:05] Priya Rao: Any SOC2/ISO attestations we can include in the listing?
[03:09] Sofia Ramos: We have SOC2 Type II and ISO 27001 artifacts; I'll put those in the doc bundle. We'll also include our standard security architecture and logging/export with SIEM hooks.
[03:20] Marco Silva: For the reference arch diagram, can you include specifics about network ports and whether customers need NAT gateways for egress to the model catalog? Some customers are locked down.
[03:33] Ethan Li: Definitely. In our reference doc we'll call out required endpoints: model catalog fetch endpoints (HTTPS), container registry access, optional telemetry endpoints if they opt-in, and KMS endpoints. For fully air-gapped deployments we have a packaging process for the model artifacts and a one-time sync. Expect some translation errors in our docs sometimes where we call KV cache "K-V cash" in older drafts, so apologies.
[03:58] Anika Patel: Haha noted. Regarding packaging — are you able to provide a single Helm chart and a Terraform module for marketplace provisioning? Our ops team likes a one-click deploy via a Marketplace ARM/Terraform template.
[04:12] Ethan Li: Yes we can provide both. The Helm chart will expose values for image repo, model variants, quantization profiles, and an option toggles for KV cache and batching. The terraform module will wire up IAM roles, VPC peering configs, and a private endpoint if needed. We'll include samples for AWS and Azure marketplaces.
[04:36] Ravi Menon: How do you recommend handling model updates and rollouts for customers who pin versions? Do you support in-place upgrades?
[04:44] Ethan Li: We support pinning model versions and can do canary rollouts or A/B with automatic fallbacks. For private deployments we ship a local model artifact registry; operators can choose automatic fetch from Redwood catalog or manual sync. We'll document upgrade steps in the runbook.
[05:05] Anika Patel: On listing metadata — we'll need descriptions, three screenshots, logos in SVG/PNG, a 200-word marketing blurb, and a contact. We'll also want the technical docs link.
[05:17] Sofia Ramos: We'll assemble that. Ethan, can you own the screenshots and runbook?
[05:22] Ethan Li: Yup, I'll own the runbook and sample chart.
[05:25] [05:30] Priya Rao: Another security Q: audit logs — can we push Redwood audit logs to customer SIEM?
[05:36] Sofia Ramos: Yes, customers can ship logs via syslog/FluentD/OTLP and we can integrate with S3 or event bridge. We also retain audit trails in the control plane; retention configurable.
[05:48] Marco Silva: For marketplace packaging, we need to test a customer flow where a Skybridge customer subscribes to the Redwood listing and then we provision a sandbox. Can Redwood trigger provisioning via a webhook?
[05:59] Ethan Li: Yes, the marketplace integration can invoke a provisioning webhook that triggers our pipeline (or you can call our API). We'll provide a provisioning template that can be executed in your marketplace orchestration.
[06:14] Anika Patel: On commercial terms, are you flexible on usage tiers for our marketplace — like per-inference vs reserved capacity?
[06:23] Sofia Ramos: We support both. For Marketplace-managed we can map plans to reserved capacity SKUs or variable per-unit pricing. For Dedicated/reserved capacity we typically do a monthly commit and map that to a marketplace plan.
[06:37] Ravi Menon: For the pilot, we'd like to run a 2-week smoke test with one customer using a Redwood Dedicated instance in our QA region. What are typical benchmarks we should expect?
[06:48] Ethan Li: For generation workloads on 8xA100 we typically see 50-80 tokens/sec depending on model and quantization; for embeddings it's higher throughput. We'll include expected latency curves in the doc. Also note that batching profiles and KV cache use significantly change throughput numbers.
[07:11] Anika Patel: Great. Let's talk technical blocker: network topology for private link — we often enforce egress-only via proxy. Does Redwood require customers to open inbound ports?
[07:22] Ethan Li: No inbound open ports to customer infra except for optional admin retreat; most integration patterns rely on outbound TLS to Redwood control endpoints or VPC peering where traffic is internal. If you want completely private connectivity, VPC peering or PrivateLink is recommended.
[07:39] Priya Rao: Do you have a recommended threat model for supply-chain risk and verifying model artifacts?
[07:46] Sofia Ramos: Yes, our reference arch includes artifact signing and checksum verification; for sensitive customers we support signed images and an SBOM for runtime components. We'll include those docs.
[07:58] Marco Silva: About the reference architecture diagram — can you show both the SaaS and the Private variant side-by-side and include the control-plane/data-plane split?
[08:07] Ethan Li: Yep, we'll produce a side-by-side diagram highlighting control-plane (Redwood) and data-plane (customer) boundaries, with clear notes on what crosses the network.
[08:19] Anika Patel: For marketplace certification, we have a security checklist; can you complete a questionnaire?
[08:25] Sofia Ramos: Absolutely. Send it over and we'll fill it in. Ethan, Maya — let's coordinate on that.
[08:31] Maya Chen: On it. We'll also include our SOC2/ISO pack.
[08:35] [08:40] Anika Patel: A few nitty-gritty items — image registries: do you require customers to use your registry or can they pull images from their private registry?
[08:48] Ethan Li: Customers can use their own private registry; we'll provide signed images and instructions to mirror images into their registry. We also support ECR/GCR/ACR examples.
[08:58] Ravi Menon: For monitoring, we want to ingest metrics into our existing Prometheus stack — is there an exporter?
[09:05] Ethan Li: Yes, the runtime exposes Prom metrics and there is an exporter. We also export traces via OTLP. We'll add config examples to the Helm chart.
[09:17] Marco Silva: A question on licensing: some customers want to self-host but have Redwood manage updates — is there a pattern where Redwood runs the control plane in our VPC but we run the data plane?
[09:29] Sofia Ramos: That's a supported hybrid model — control plane in a tenant-specific VPC or our managed control plane with a strong peering relationship; we can discuss legal and SLA implications.
[09:40] Anika Patel: For the marketplace listing page, we need a short video showing the onboarding flow. Can Redwood provide a 90s demo video?
[09:48] Sofia Ramos: Yes, we'll capture a 90-120s walkthrough of the marketplace subscribe and provision flow. Ethan to record the demo.
[09:55] Ethan Li: I'll record and send a link.
[09:58] [10:10] Priya Rao: Encryption at rest — do you provide per-customer encryption keys or a shared key per deployment?
[10:18] Ethan Li: For private deployments we always recommend per-customer keys via KMS; hosted deployments can use per-tenant keys when required. We'll outline defaults and options.
[10:30] Anika Patel: For testing the provisioning webhook, do you prefer we spin up a test marketplace tenant or share staging creds?
[10:38] Marco Silva: We can spin up a staging tenant, but we'll need Redwood to provide a staging subscription flow to validate end-to-end.
[10:45] Sofia Ramos: Fine, we'll ask product ops to create a staging flow and a sample payload for the webhook.
[10:52] [11:10] Anika Patel: Let's talk ownership for docs — who will host the reference architecture? We prefer the vendor provide a canonical doc we can link to.
[11:18] Sofia Ramos: Redwood will host the canonical reference arch and runbook on our docs site and provide a markdown bundle for you to mirror. We'll include diagrams in PNG/SVG and a machine-readable terraform module.
[11:30] Marco Silva: Are there any known issues with Azure Marketplace that we should watch for?
[11:36] Ethan Li: Azure sometimes requires additional manifest metadata and has a stricter VM image validation for private offers; we'll include an Azure-specific checklist.
[11:44] Ravi Menon: For the cookbooks — any recommended defaults for autoscaling thresholds and batching windows?
[11:52] Ethan Li: We'll include defaults: target p99 latency thresholds, batching windows (20-100ms), and suggestions on quantization profiles by model size. Note that CPU vs GPU differences matter; we'll call out recommended GPU types per workload.
[12:10] [12:40] Anika Patel: Ok this is super helpful. Do we need any additional security review from Redwood legal before the listing?
[12:47] Sofia Ramos: Most marketplaces require a standard commercial agreement; we can share a marketplace-ready contract. For anything bespoke we'll loop legal.
[12:55] Priya Rao: One more — for audit logs we need retention controls, can we set retention to 90 days or 1 year?
[13:03] Sofia Ramos: Yes retention is configurable; we'll surface how to set that in the runbook.
[13:12] [13:30] Anika Patel: Good. Let's recap next steps — share checklist, send runbook, get legal contacts, schedule follow-up.
[13:38] Sofia Ramos: Great. Ethan — you'll handle the runbook and Helm chart. Maya will share SOC docs. Marco to provide Skybridge marketplace ops contact.
[13:48] Ethan Li: Yep.
[13:52] Marco Silva: I'll send contact and an initial test tenant setup.
[13:56] [14:10] Anika Patel: Final Q from my side — pricing visibility on the listing, do you want prices displayed or contact sales?
[14:18] Sofia Ramos: We typically list starting price bands and have an enterprise contact; flexible.
[14:24] Anika Patel: Okay thanks everyone. We'll get those artifacts and plan the demo the week of 2026-04-20.
[14:32] Sofia Ramos: Thanks all. We'll follow up via email with the checklist. Bye.
[14:38] [END] 

Notes: transcript contains some minor transcription artifacts (occasional mis-heard words, slight punctuation inconsistencies) as typical from Fireflies exports. References to KV cache sometimes rendered oddly in older docs. Links mentioned during the call: "redwood-docs/reference-arch" (internal link), "redwood-samples/helm-chart" (artifact).
